rule_schema.legacy_default_policy: Existing badcase_rules without v2 fields inherit defaults from the audit rule registry until they are migrated.

protected_rhythm: title, contents, section divider, content, and closing rhythm
key message card plus numbered claim/support blocks
do not inherit rounded proof-panel polish unless the style contract explicitly changes
warm paper background with restrained teal, gold, and clay accents
one claim plus one proof object per content slide
green proof type badge stays at the panel corner while black identity label anchors to fitted content
straight rectangular left claim panel pairs cleanly with straight rectangular right evidence panel
right-side large figure is preferred when it preserves readability
white research-board canvas with faint vertical grid lines and a restrained top rail
straight rectangular claim and evidence containers with crisp academic spacing
large left claim panel plus large right evidence panel for premise/mechanism text evidence
full-width top claim band plus wide lower proof panel for figure/table evidence pages
evidence area should feel used, not decorative or empty

accepted_reference.reason: Human reviewer preferred v5 over v6; v5 is the current aesthetic checkpoint before further automation work.

protected_traits: Contents page uses the six-module route: Motivation, Method, Analysis, Ablations, Results, Conclusion
title, contents, section divider, content slide, and closing rhythm
Key message card plus numbered claim/support blocks
bottom-table pages keep a populated right evidence region when no figure is present

legacy_visual_reference.note: Preserved as legacy original-academic visual evidence. Its four-module Contents page should not override the mHC six-module structure rule.

golden_baseline1_reference.reason: The from-scratch warm academic style survived Kimi K2 primary iteration, mHC cross-paper validation, and DeepSeek_V4 figure/table/text proof-panel micro-polish; the reviewer considered v25 satisfactory enough to preserve as a second golden reference.
golden_baseline1_reference.relationship_to_original_golden_baseline: Do not replace the mature academic golden baseline. Use golden_baseline1 as an independent from-scratch style reference and as a benchmark-driven self-repair target.
protected_style_traits: warm paper background with restrained teal/gold/clay accents
academic title, agenda, section, content, and closing rhythm
one claim plus one proof object per content slide
rounded proof panels whose green type badge stays at the panel corner
black proof identity labels anchored to the underlying figure, table, metric, or explanation text
figure/table/caption geometry driven by the fitted content box rather than by the rounded panel alone

golden_baseline2_reference.reason: The blind rectangular research-board style was iterated with style-aware benchmark checks and human feedback until the reviewer accepted its visual rhythm. It is preserved as a human-tuned frozen reference, not as proof of a fully autonomous style proposal loop.
protected_style_traits: faint vertical grid background and restrained top rail
large evidence panels that should be visually used rather than left empty
focused table views with top label and centered explanatory note

frozen_reference_suite.principle: Frozen references are evaluation baselines and regression targets. Autonomous proposal routes must not read their complete PPTX files, full style contracts, or layout grammars.

autonomous_style_proposal_policy.goal: Generate new style_contract + layout grammar from paper content and abstract design primitives, then enter bounded repair loop.
forbidden_inputs: golden_baseline0 academic PPTX or full layout grammar
golden_baseline1 PPTX or full rounded proof-panel style contract
golden_baseline2 PPTX or full straight-rectangle research-board style contract
any extracted page template copied from frozen references

stop_conditions: no high or medium findings remain
two consecutive iterations do not improve multidimensional score
repair triggers metric_improved_visual_regressed or human rejection

forbidden_content: style-specific exact measurements copied from frozen references

sixway_smoke_benchmark_plan.paper_policy: Use one user-provided paper that has not been parsed before; parse once, reuse checkpoints for all routes.
smoke_pass_criteria: all routes produce slides.pptx and speaker_script.md
autonomous routes produce style_contract and forbidden_reference_attestation
at least one autonomous route clears high and medium findings within three repair iterations
human review outcomes can be written back as scoped rules
sixway_smoke_benchmark_plan.scale_after_smoke: Run five papers covering figure-heavy, table-heavy, metric-heavy, system-diagram-heavy, and text-heavy cases before considering ten papers or ai20.

autonomy_levels.L0_manual_template: Human directly designs or edits the deck/template.
autonomy_levels.L1_agent_renders_given_template: Agent renders paper content into a provided complete template.
autonomy_levels.L2_human_feedback_guided_repair: Agent renders/repairs, but human names the main badcases.
autonomy_levels.L3_benchmark_guided_multi_round_repair: Agent repairs with existing rules across multiple iterations; human spot-checks.
autonomy_levels.L4_autonomous_style_proposal_and_repair: Agent proposes a new style without reading complete golden templates and completes bounded repair.

sample_observations.observation: Pages appear as 512x512 raster images, which weakens editability and text extraction even if the visual result looks polished.
Text is extractable and structure is clear, but editing requires LaTeX rather than native PowerPoint object manipulation.

candidate_style_reference.reason: Human reviewer considered Kimi K2 v10 successful; subsequent mHC and DeepSeek_V4 validation converted cross-paper failures into badcases and repairs, culminating in DeepSeek_V4 v25 as the preserved golden_baseline1 artifact.
promotion_criteria: passes nonvisual audit with no high or medium findings on at least two non-Kimi papers
human review confirms the style still feels polished when figures, tables, and evidence density differ
new cross-paper failures are converted into badcases before promotion

validation_cases.finding_summary: 56 low findings; no high or medium findings after wide-figure aspect-aware reflow, inline-table payload indexing, shallow-card internal spacing, agenda read-path header clearance, and table support band balance repairs.
56 low findings; no high or medium findings after centering non-figure proof identity labels over their underlying content.
Deep Residual fresh parse produced 60 findings: 2 high, 0 medium, 58 low. Kept as scoped validation evidence, not as a replacement for DeepSeek_V4 v25.

self_generated_style_candidates.reason: The blind loop created an independent style without reusing original academic or golden_baseline1 visual grammar. It is useful as a preserved self-generated candidate even though it still has unresolved audit findings.
promotion_criteria: passes at least two additional fresh-paper smoke tests
reduces high and medium findings through benchmark-driven self-repair
human reviewer accepts the style rhythm as distinct and useful
new recurring failures are converted into scoped badcases before promotion

script_generation_policy.rule: Speaker scripts are route-specific artifacts rather than one shared paper-level script.
why: original academic, golden_baseline1, and blind experimental decks present the same paper through different visual grammars and evidence rhythms
the script should cue the presenter to the actual proof object, title rhythm, and evidence board used on that route
minimum_audit_checks: slide count in script matches PPTX slide count
script headings cover the actual slide titles
generic placeholder narration fragments are rejected
blind experimental scripts retain explicit evidence cues

semantic_quality_badcases.trigger: numbered point or slide title is an unfinished clause or boilerplate prefix such as 'The paper addresses the problem of' or 'In short'
semantic_quality_badcases.repair: rebuild the claim from the supporting sentence into a complete idea phrase

semantic_quality_badcases.trigger: metric card contains a bare small number with a generic label such as 'Accuracy', often caused by dataset/model names like CIFAR-10 or ResNet-50
semantic_quality_badcases.repair: drop the card or replace it with a sourced value that has units, percent, or explicit benchmark context

core_principles.rule: Do not reparse a paper when summary, plan, slide_spec, figures, tables, and metrics are already available and reliable.
core_principles.why: The Kimi K2 parsing chain was already strong; from-scratch means a new slide story and visual system, not a new PDF understanding pass.

core_principles.rule: Build a content-complete inventory and rough slide story before optimizing aesthetics.
core_principles.why: A good-looking deck that drops tables, metrics, or proof objects fails the paper-reading task.

core_principles.rule: Choose the presentation archetype, deck structure, layout families, proof-object grammar, and component composition before tuning font sizes or local text density.
core_principles.why: The successful v5 iteration came from first establishing an academic paper-reading style system; v6 showed that local component resizing can hurt the whole-slide composition.

core_principles.rule: Keep typography roles deck-consistent, then fit real text into each component; if a local component becomes clearly too empty or too full, resize that component and reflow its same-slide siblings.
core_principles.why: v9 showed that single-page text tweaks are not enough: component size, internal spacing, and local page composition form one loop after content is inserted.

core_principles.rule: Every subjective complaint should be translated into a badcase, trigger signal, repair strategy, and regression check.
core_principles.why: The goal is not one manually corrected PPT, but a benchmark that helps future decks self-diagnose and improve.

core_principles.rule: For the current phase, use PPTX geometry, text, font, table, and layout metadata only; do not render pages or call a vision model.
core_principles.why: The user prefers preserving good component composition and avoiding costly screenshot/vision loops; metadata checks can catch many text, overlap, and density risks.

core_principles.rule: If an automatic heuristic produces a version the human reviewer dislikes, preserve the preferred version and record the heuristic as risky.
core_principles.why: v6 tried to optimize read path and sparse evidence cards, but the user found v5 better overall.

core_principles.rule: A style that succeeds on one paper becomes a candidate reference, not a golden baseline, until it passes other papers with different evidence shapes.
core_principles.why: A visual system can fit one paper's content distribution while failing on denser figures, different tables, or less regular proof objects.

core_principles.rule: Every badcase should declare whether it is global, mature-baseline-specific, golden-baseline1-specific, or experimental-style-specific before it is allowed to auto-repair a deck.
core_principles.why: Rules learned from rounded proof panels can improve golden_baseline1 while harming the original academic golden baseline if they are applied without checking the active style contract.

core_principles.rule: New benchmark or repair rules must be tested on the original golden baseline, golden_baseline1, and at least one fresh-paper trial before they become default auto-repair behavior.
core_principles.why: The benchmark is intended to protect style quality across templates, not force every template into the latest successful visual grammar.

core_principles.rule: Autonomous style proposal may use abstract design primitives but must not read complete golden reference templates or layout recipes.
core_principles.why: This gives the agent design vocabulary without letting it simply copy human-tuned golden baselines.

core_principles.rule: Human feedback turns, marked slides, rule conversion, and human outcomes are first-class benchmark data.
core_principles.why: Human-in-the-loop should be quantified as the system moves from L2 guided repair toward L4 autonomous proposal.

core_principles.rule: Academic, golden_baseline1, and golden_baseline2 are evaluation references and regression targets, not proposal templates.
core_principles.why: The next benchmark must distinguish reusable human-tuned baselines from truly autonomous new style generation.

human_findings: No academic title slide.
No agenda / roadmap slide.
Most pages repeated a large right-side proof panel.
Short text evidence appeared inside oversized empty panels.
Tables were sometimes summarized instead of rendered as complete table evidence.
The system lacked a deck-render review loop.
repairs: Add title, agenda, section, and closing slides.
Introduce layout families beyond a single right proof panel.
Treat figures, tables, text evidence, and metrics as distinct proof objects.
Add visual audit manifest and render-review hook.

human_findings: Black-and-white palette felt dull and lifeless.
Cover black bar and meaningless metric chips looked unattractive.
Agenda number buttons were too heavy.
Some limitation / motivation / method evidence panels remained sparse.
Some table and card components overlapped body text.
Metric layouts were inconsistent across pages.
repairs: Switch to warm academic palette with teal, soft gold, clay, and paper tones.
Replace heavy black cover treatment with a lighter cover system.
Replace agenda dots with module markers and a deck map.
Route short proof text to compact evidence cards.
Add table-bottom review targets and overlap-oriented badcase rules.

human_findings: The deck became much better aesthetically.
Cover right rail should show paper highlights, not only source inventory counts.
Evidence-note triplets repeated too often and needed more variation.
A table panel still overlapped support text on one page.
Some body text felt too small or sparse.
repairs: Derive cover-ready paper highlights from existing checkpoints.
Vary evidence card layouts: right stack, bottom notes, mosaic, and compact cards.
Move table panels below claim/support text with clear gutters.
Add text snapshot fallback for review when PNG rendering is unavailable.

human_findings: Cover paper highlights were good, but source-depth chips at the bottom were unnecessary.
Agenda read path should use visual flow components instead of dry text.
A three-card evidence mosaic needed better proportions.
Left-side evidence triplets felt less formal than right or bottom placement.
PowerPoint rendering still had local COM reliability issues.
repairs: Remove cover source-depth chips and keep paper highlights prominent.
Use compact read-path nodes instead of a plain text arrow chain.
Prefer right-side and bottom evidence placements; avoid left evidence triplets for formal academic pages.
Keep renderer failures explicit and continue exporting text snapshots.

human_findings: This version was considered the most pleasing checkpoint.
The deck should be saved before further experiments.
repairs: Treat rough_draft_v5 as the current accepted benchmark reference.
Use v5 as the regression target for future aesthetic changes.

human_findings: v6 was less attractive than v5 and felt strange.
The 2x2 read path and aggressive sparse-card resizing did not improve the overall deck.
repairs: Rollback v6 visual heuristics.
Record that local density optimization can hurt composition and should require human or visual-regression approval.

human_findings: Cover highlight bodies sat too far below their labels, weakening the colored-rail pairing.
The agenda read path correctly wrapped to two rows, but the columns were too far apart and labels were not visually anchored under nodes.
Bottom evidence cards could become too tall after text fitting; this should be treated as local component reflow, not deck-wide font drift.
Figure component labels sat too close to rounded panel boundaries.
repairs: Add paired label-body spacing checks for cover highlight rail stacks.
Add 2x2 read-path grid checks for column gap, row gap, and label-center drift.
Add content-fit component frame checks so sparse cards can shrink locally and trigger same-slide reflow.
Add component label boundary-inset checks for figure/table proof panels.

human_findings: Human reviewer considered the v10 PPT very successful and aesthetically satisfying on the Kimi K2 primary case.
The current style should be preserved as a candidate reference but not promoted to golden baseline before cross-paper validation.
repairs: Record v10 as a candidate style reference with promotion criteria instead of replacing the accepted v5 checkpoint immediately.
Use the mHC paper as the next validation case for detecting cross-paper style failures.
Keep the human-in-the-loop loop active: generate, inspect, translate complaints into badcases, then repair and rerun.

human_findings: Directly applying the v10 visual style to mHC initially produced many text overflow findings because mHC claims, author list, highlights, and conclusion evidence are longer and more theoretical.
The style grammar itself did not trigger geometry or optical-balance failures after repair; the main cross-paper issue was text compression and narrow-card fitting.
repairs: Add cross-paper claim/support word limits by proof type.
Compact long author lists on cover slides.
Remove Kimi-specific closing copy and derive closing takeaway from paper highlights.
Route non-metric closing summaries to evidence cards instead of metric grids.
Use compact typography for narrow evidence-card stacks.

human_findings: Wide figures such as Figure 4 and Figure 6 were forced into the generic right-side rounded rectangle, making long horizontal diagrams visually unclear and sometimes distorted.
A slide_spec inline table with real rows was referenced by its display title, but the renderer only indexed extracted asset-table ids, so the proof panel fell back to a near-empty text block.
repairs: Route figure proof objects by source image aspect ratio: very wide figures use a long bottom proof panel rather than a side proof panel.
Fit figure images into their content box while preserving the original aspect ratio.
Index curated inline table rows alongside extracted asset tables so title-referenced tables still render as native PPT tables.
Add benchmark badcases for wide-figure layout mismatch and inline table payload indexing failures.

human_findings: On the conclusion slide, the right-side evidence note cards were shallower than earlier evidence cards, but they reused the same fixed label/body offsets.
The labels looked acceptable, yet the body text sat too low inside each rounded card because internal spacing did not adapt to the local card height.
repairs: Add a compact-shallow evidence card mode that reduces label/body gap and gives the body text a taller box inside shallow cards.
Add a nonvisual audit rule for shallow evidence cards whose internal label/body spacing or bottom padding does not scale to the frame.
Record the lesson that component internals must be proportional to local component size, not only globally consistent by component type.

human_findings: The mHC v12 deck was considered essentially finished, but the agenda Read path header felt slightly too close to the P/M/E/T flow nodes.
This is a low-risk polish issue: it does not break structure, but it weakens the small rail's hierarchy and breathing room.
repairs: Lift the agenda Read path header while preserving the existing two-row flow node grid.
Add a metadata-only audit rule for Read path header-to-node clearance so this kind of final polish can be tracked without screenshot review.
Record that not every human discomfort needs a major repair; some become scoped micro-polish rules.

human_findings: On table interpretation slides 26 and 28, the support explanation felt too close to the table panel and too far from the bold claim.
The page had no collision or table extraction failure, but the support copy's vertical center of gravity was pulled downward by the table proof object.
repairs: Move table-bottom support copy closer to the claim and lower the table panel enough to preserve a visible gutter.
Add a metadata-only audit rule for table-bottom claim/support/table-panel spacing.
Record that table pages need a text-band balance check, not only overlap and native-table row checks.

human_findings: The v14 style could be generated from existing DeepSeek_V4 checkpoints without new model calls, but nonvisual audit caught high-risk overflow in long proof captions.
DeepSeek_V4 figure captions are substantially longer than the mHC caption payloads, so fixed-height caption boxes need capacity-aware truncation.
repairs: Add capacity-aware proof-caption fitting based on caption box width, height, and font size.
Use a slightly smaller cover title size for very long paper titles.
Record DeepSeek_V4 as another cross-paper validation case for the candidate style.

human_findings: Tall figures such as Figure 1 and Figure 7 were preserved in aspect ratio but placed inside near-square side panels, making the figures feel visually compressed and too small.
Medium-wide figures such as Figure 5 were still routed to ordinary side panels because the previous threshold only caught very wide figures.
Bottom wide figures such as Figure 6 used the right macro-layout, but the FIGURE/Figure label row consumed vertical space that should have belonged to the image.
repairs: Route tall figures to vertical proof panels and medium-wide/wide figures to horizontal bottom proof panels based on source image aspect ratio.
Move FIGURE and Figure N labels out of the image's top row so the image viewport can use more of the proof panel height.
Add a metadata-only audit rule for figure panel aspect mismatch, separate from picture aspect distortion.

human_findings: The v16 side label rail repaired image height but made the slides uglier because the labels reserved a full left column and pushed the image away from the proof panel center.
Some only mildly-wide figures were sent to bottom horizontal panels; the bottom-wide threshold was too permissive.
Figure captions inside wide and tall proof panels should span the panel width and be centered, not be constrained by the label area.
repairs: Raise the bottom-wide figure threshold so only figures at least about 1.9x wider than tall use the bottom horizontal panel.
Treat figure labels as compact annotations rather than reserved layout columns; center the image and caption in the full rounded panel.
Let side proof panels extend lower when the source footer lives on the opposite side, and move the footer away from left-side proof panels.

human_findings: On bottom-wide figure slides, FIGURE/Figure N labels were still anchored to the panel corner instead of the fitted image, leaving unnecessary top whitespace and making the image feel lower than the proof panel.
Side tall figure panels benefited from a taller frame, but horizontal Figure N labels repeated the green FIGURE label and did not attach tightly enough to the image.
When a left-side figure panel consumes the left bottom area, the source footer should move to the open right-bottom side and align right.
repairs: Compute the fitted image rectangle first, then anchor bottom-wide FIGURE/Figure N labels to the image's left edge above the image.
Use a vertical Figure N label only for side tall figure panels, with its top aligned to the image top while the green FIGURE label remains compact above the image.
Expand tall side proof panels slightly downward and keep source footers right-aligned on the open side.
Keep caption boxes fixed-height and apply stricter capacity-aware truncation so captions do not grow outside rounded proof panels.

human_findings: The green FIGURE badge describes the rounded proof panel type, not the fitted source image, so placing it directly above the image misuses the visual grammar.
Putting the green FIGURE badge and the black Figure N identity label in the same row above the image creates crowding and pushes the Figure N label off its intended optical anchor.

Bottom-wide and side-tall figure panels should use the same semantic split: FIGURE stays inside the rounded panel's top-left corner, while Figure N becomes a vertical image identity label near the fitted image's upper-left side.
repairs: Pin the green FIGURE badge to the rounded figure panel's inner top-left corner for both side-tall and bottom-wide figure panels.
Render Figure N as a vertical identity label beside the fitted image, top-aligned near the image instead of sharing a horizontal title row with the green badge.
Add a metadata-only audit rule and badcase for figure badge / identity-label conflation so future decks catch this regression without screenshots or model calls.

human_findings: The intended left-side Figure N label is not a rotated 'Figure N' string; it should be true stacked text: F / I / G / U / R / E / N.
The stacked Figure N identity label should sit closer to the fitted image's left edge than the previous rotated label.
repairs:
Render the identity label as explicit multi-line text such as F
I
G
U
R
E
7 instead of using PowerPoint rotation.
Move the stacked identity label closer to the fitted image while keeping it inside the figure panel.
Tighten the metadata audit so rotated 'Figure N' text is still reported even if its bbox is vertical.

human_findings: True stacked F/I/G/U/R/E/N labels were technically faithful to the previous wording but looked worse than the original horizontal Figure N label.
The preferred compromise is to keep Figure N horizontal, outside the image, just above and left-aligned to the fitted image's upper-left corner.
This feedback is a caution that literal vertical text can overcorrect a spacing issue and hurt visual taste.
repairs: Revert the image identity label to horizontal Figure N text while keeping the green FIGURE badge at the panel's inner top-left corner.
Anchor horizontal Figure N to the fitted image's upper-left outside edge with a small vertical gap.
Add a badcase for stacked_figure_identity_label_overcorrection so future repair passes do not reintroduce the stacked label.

human_findings: Placing Figure N at the image's upper-left outside corner is workable but still too close to the green FIGURE badge on side tall panels.
The preferred micro-polish is to keep Figure N horizontal and place it centered above the fitted image so it separates from the panel badge.
repairs: Center the horizontal Figure N label above the fitted image.
Keep the green FIGURE panel badge unchanged at the rounded panel's inner top-left corner.
Update metadata audit to check Figure N center alignment against the fitted image centerline.

human_findings: The Figure N textbox was centered above the fitted image, but the paragraph remained left-aligned inside the textbox, so the visible text still looked off-center.
The intended alignment target is the fitted image itself, not the rounded proof panel.
repairs: Center-align the Figure N paragraph inside the textbox after centering the textbox above the fitted image.
Add a badcase for figure_label_text_alignment_off_center so metadata audit catches centered boxes with left-aligned visible text.

human_findings: Slide 12 used the generic visual_left figure proof panel, where Figure N was still rendered as a wide left-aligned title row rather than visible text centered above the fitted image.
The same issue can recur in visual_left and visual_right layouts whenever a normal-aspect figure is routed through the generic proof-object renderer.
repairs: Route generic figure proof panels through the same fitted-image label placement used by wide and tall figure panels.
Extend metadata audit beyond wide/tall figure panel aspects so any rounded panel with FIGURE/Figure N semantics and a picture checks the Figure N image-center anchor and paragraph alignment.

human_findings: Non-figure proof panels had the same visual problem: black identity labels such as Motivation, Method, Doc Table 1, and Table 2 were left-aligned in a header row instead of being visually centered over the underlying explanation text or table.
The desired target is the main panel content, not the rounded rectangle itself; green type badges remain panel-corner labels.
repairs: Center proof identity labels over the underlying content box for text evidence, table, and metric proof panels.
Add metadata audit rules for panel_identity_label_anchor_drift and panel_identity_label_text_alignment_off_center.

style_scope_policy.mature_academic_baseline_policy: Run new rules as warnings first. Do not auto-apply golden_baseline1 rounded-panel repairs to the original academic golden baseline unless the deck contains the same rounded proof-panel grammar and the original baseline regression suite passes.
style_scope_policy.promotion_gate: A rule can become default auto-repair only after it improves or preserves academic, golden_baseline1, golden_baseline2, and at least one autonomous fresh-paper trial.
style_scope_policy.autonomous_proposal_policy: Autonomous proposal routes may use abstract primitives and badcase triggers, but must not auto-copy full frozen reference layout grammars.

trigger_signals: deck has no title role slide
first slide lacks paper title
badcase_rules.root_cause: Paper-reading deck was treated as content pages only.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Always generate a polished academic title slide.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Slide 1 has role=title and includes paper title, author/team, and a concise deck thesis.

trigger_signals: no agenda / roadmap slide
sections are not visible before content slides
badcase_rules.root_cause: Narrative planning was not reflected in the PPT.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Generate a roadmap page from section buckets and slide counts.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Slide 2 has role=agenda and lists Motivation, Method, Experiments, and Takeaways or equivalent paper-specific modules.

trigger_signals: dominant layout family ratio > 0.45
max consecutive same layout >= 4
large proof panel appears in the same position on most slides
badcase_rules.root_cause: Renderer reused one macro layout for unrelated evidence types.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Rotate layout families by role and proof type: right proof, bottom proof, table bottom, metric cards, evidence stack, evidence mosaic.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Visual audit reports varied layout families and no long run of identical content layouts.

trigger_signals: proof_object.type == text_evidence
proof text is short
assigned proof panel area is large
badcase_rules.root_cause: Short text evidence was treated like a figure/table proof object.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Use compact evidence notes, bottom cards, or mosaic cards instead of a large empty proof panel.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Short evidence pages do not show mostly empty oversized rounded rectangles.

trigger_signals: table proof object exists
native table has no parsed rows
slide only contains a textual table summary
badcase_rules.root_cause: Table extraction was not carried through to the renderer.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Preserve parsed table rows in content inventory and render them as native PPT tables.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Table proof slides show row/column grammar and include at least one non-header row when source rows exist.

trigger_signals: table or proof panel intersects body text box
shape bounding boxes overlap above threshold
render review shows text covered by card/panel
badcase_rules.root_cause: Proof object y-position or height did not reserve enough gutter for claim/support text.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Move proof panels lower, reduce proof height, or split content across alternate layouts.
badcase_rules.regression_check: No high-risk overlap among title, claim, support, table, and proof panel bounding boxes.

trigger_signals: palette uses mostly black, white, and gray
section dividers use full dark backgrounds repeatedly
accent colors are absent or semantically unused
badcase_rules.root_cause: Academic restraint was interpreted as monochrome.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Use a restrained warm academic palette with semantic accents.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Deck uses warm paper background plus 2-3 muted accent colors without becoming over-decorated.

trigger_signals: cover highlights only counts figures/tables/metrics
cover side rail lacks paper-specific contribution summary
badcase_rules.root_cause: Cover used source inventory rather than paper value proposition.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Derive 3 paper highlights from parsed checkpoints: core result, scale, design edge, or evidence scope.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Cover side rail includes paper-specific highlights, not just source-depth counters.

trigger_signals: agenda right panel contains only plain arrow text
read path has no visual rhythm
badcase_rules.root_cause: Narrative flow was rendered as dry copy instead of a component.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Use compact flow nodes/icons while preserving balance; do not overcomplicate if the panel becomes awkward.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Agenda side panel shows readable flow components and does not feel crowded.

trigger_signals: new heuristic shrinks or rearranges cards but human preference worsens
visual composition feels less stable than accepted reference
badcase_rules.root_cause: A local non-visual metric optimized sparse text boxes but ignored whole-slide composition.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Gate density-based visual changes behind accepted-reference comparison and selective rendered review.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Changes that alter accepted v5 visual grammar require either improved visual score or explicit human approval.

trigger_signals: support/body role font size is below metadata floor
support/body role font size falls below preferred band while capacity is safe
badcase_rules.root_cause: A readable academic composition was kept, but secondary prose was authored with too little typographic presence.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Increase body/support font size, improve hierarchy, or shorten copy before changing the component box.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Body/support text clears the metadata floor and no new near-overflow finding is introduced.

trigger_signals: evidence card body font size is below metadata floor
cover highlight or evidence note body sits below preferred font band
badcase_rules.root_cause: Compact evidence cards preserved the v5 composition but made card copy feel underpowered.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Raise card label/body typography within the existing card group and split notes only if capacity becomes risky.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Evidence card text clears the card font floor while card group geometry remains close to the accepted reference.

trigger_signals: claim/support/card text roles are too close in font size
component labels visually compete with evidence body text
badcase_rules.root_cause: The slide has the right components but insufficient type contrast between claim, support, labels, and notes.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Adjust font hierarchy and weight first; avoid moving components unless overlap or capacity fails.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Claim remains dominant, support is readable, and card body text has clearer hierarchy.

trigger_signals: low_text_density finding on evidence card text
card copy has very few words while the card group has accepted geometry
badcase_rules.root_cause: A card sized for a reading note received a thin label or fragment instead of useful evidence copy.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Enrich the card body from existing support/proof text or rebalance reading notes; do not shrink the whole card group.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Card information density improves without changing the accepted component composition.

trigger_signals: evidence cards have strongly uneven word counts
one note is near capacity while a sibling card is sparse
badcase_rules.root_cause: Support text was split mechanically instead of being allocated to balanced reading notes.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Redistribute note copy, shorten the dense card, and enrich sparse siblings before resizing cards.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Sibling card word counts move into a comparable range and no overflow finding appears.

trigger_signals: a repair changes component size or position when only low-density findings were present
no overlap, out-of-bounds, unreadable table, or repeated-layout structural finding exists
badcase_rules.root_cause: The repair loop treated low density as a geometry problem and risked repeating the v6 regression.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Reject geometry changes unless a structural finding exists; prefer typography, line breaks, copy allocation, or notes splitting.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Low-density-only repairs preserve component geometry and update only typography/copy fields.

trigger_signals: cover title/support metadata remains below the cover comfort font band
right highlight rail typography is lifted but left title narrative is not lifted as a group
badcase_rules.root_cause: Cover typography was tuned per component, so the right rail could improve while the left title, author, thesis, and focus copy stayed visually underpowered.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Lift the cover's left-side typography as one hierarchy group, then recheck wrapping and vertical spacing before moving components.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Cover left title narrative clears the comfort band and no new wrap, overlap, or out-of-bounds warning appears.

trigger_signals: agenda read-path labels sit in one row with too little horizontal gap
four compact flow buttons are squeezed into a narrow side panel
badcase_rules.root_cause: The flow component only knew one horizontal layout and did not choose a two-row arrangement when labels became crowded.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Switch compact flow nodes to a 2x2 or two-row path when label gaps fall below the comfort threshold; do not solve this by shrinking labels.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Read-path node labels have comfortable gaps or use two rows while preserving the P/M/E/T sequence.

trigger_signals: a rounded container has strongly uneven top and bottom padding around its internal content stack
metric or evidence cards occupy only the upper or lower part of their parent panel
badcase_rules.root_cause: The audit treated each textbox separately and did not evaluate the visual center of the grouped text/card stack inside a container.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Rebalance the internal stack or enrich sparse cards before changing the whole slide macro-layout; allow slight optical bias for emphasized values.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Container text/card stacks stay within the optical padding tolerance without forcing mathematically perfect centering.

trigger_signals: metric value and label are positioned with a card-height proportional gap
two text lines inside one metric card feel disconnected after the card gets taller
badcase_rules.root_cause: Metric card internals used fixed y ratios rather than a value+label text stack with a stable gap.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Lay out metric value and label as one optical text stack with a fixed gap; keep the value slightly dominant rather than blindly centering both lines.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Metric cards preserve value dominance while the value-label gap remains within the stack comfort threshold.

trigger_signals: many slides have below-ideal typography findings even though no individual slide has a severe font violation
support, card body, or cover metadata repeatedly feels slightly too small across the deck
badcase_rules.root_cause: Low-severity typography warnings were ranked locally, so a deck-wide weak type scale never became a repair target.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Run a deck-level typography pass that safely lifts repeated roles, checks capacity, then repairs line breaks or copy allocation if needed.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Deck-level below-ideal typography count decreases without introducing near-overflow, overlap, or geometry-only repairs.

trigger_signals: a label and its explanatory body belong to the same semantic rail but their starts are too far apart
colored marker, label, and explanation no longer read as one grouped item
badcase_rules.root_cause: Typography repair lifted or moved text boxes independently instead of treating label and explanation as one optical stack.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Move the body closer to the label within the same rail group before moving the whole group or changing font size.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Cover highlight label-body top delta stays within the paired-stack threshold while each group still aligns with its colored rail.

trigger_signals: 2x2 read-path nodes have an overly wide column gap
row gap is too tight after wrapping
node labels are not centered under their circles
badcase_rules.root_cause: The repair knew to wrap the flow into two rows but did not define grid proportions and label anchoring rules.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Use a compact 2x2 flow grid with smaller column gap, larger row gap, and label boxes centered on node centers.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Read-path grid passes column-gap, row-gap, column-to-row ratio, and label-center tolerance checks.

trigger_signals: agenda slide contains a Read path header
Read path header bottom is too close to the first-row flow nodes
human reviewer describes the rail as slightly cramped even though node alignment is correct
badcase_rules.root_cause: The flow grid was repaired for node/label alignment, but the local header-to-flow breathing room was not part of the component contract.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Lift the Read path header slightly while preserving the existing flow node grid and right rail composition.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Agenda Read path header clears the nearest P/M/E/T node by the configured minimum gap.

trigger_signals: table_bottom slide contains a bold claim, support paragraph, and bottom table proof panel
support paragraph is farther from the claim than the configured claim/support gap
support paragraph is too close to the table panel top even though no overlap occurs
badcase_rules.root_cause: The table proof panel was positioned only to avoid collision, so the support copy could sit optically low between the claim and table.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Treat claim and support as one upper text band, then lower the table panel enough to preserve a visible gutter.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Table-bottom pages pass claim/support gap and support/table-panel gutter checks while preserving native table rows.

trigger_signals: figure or table proof focus text is copied into a short caption box
caption estimated text fill ratio exceeds the overflow threshold
cross-paper validation paper has longer figure captions than the primary style paper
badcase_rules.root_cause: Proof captions reused fixed-height boxes while accepting arbitrary-length source figure or table descriptions.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Limit proof captions by estimated box capacity using caption width, height, and font size; keep the full caption in source evidence rather than the visible caption.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Generated proof captions no longer trigger estimated_text_overflow while figure/table proof objects remain present.

trigger_signals: a card frame remains much taller than the fitted label/body stack
local evidence card feels empty after text has been inserted
badcase_rules.root_cause: The system froze component dimensions before seeing the real text, then tried to judge the result only by font size or text density.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Keep deck-wide typography roles stable, shrink or expand the affected local frame after content fitting, and reflow sibling components on the same slide.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Card frame extra height stays within the fitted-text threshold and sibling card alignment remains coherent.

trigger_signals: a shallow narrow evidence card reuses the same label/body offsets as taller or wider cards
body text bottom padding is too small inside a card
label appears acceptable but body text feels visually low or detached in the local frame
badcase_rules.root_cause: Component internals were governed by fixed offsets per card type rather than spacing rules that respond to the local card height.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Use a height-aware compact card mode for shallow narrow cards: reduce label/body gap, increase body text box height, and preserve deck-wide typography roles.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Shallow narrow evidence cards pass label/body gap and bottom-padding checks without changing unrelated evidence card layouts.

trigger_signals: figure/table label sits too close to a rounded panel edge
component heading appears to cross or kiss the boundary curve
badcase_rules.root_cause: Proof-object labels were placed by a fixed small offset without accounting for rounded-corner optical padding.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Inset proof-object labels farther from rounded panel corners and reduce the content viewport if needed.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Figure/table component labels clear the minimum boundary inset before figure/table content is fitted.

trigger_signals: candidate style passes the primary paper but produces high text overflow findings on another paper
long author lists, theoretical claims, dense support paragraphs, or conclusion evidence exceed the fixed style frames
non-metric closing evidence is routed into metric card grammar
badcase_rules.root_cause: The visual style was reusable, but the text compression contract was tuned to the primary paper's content shape.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Set claim/support/highlight word limits by proof type, compact long author lists, derive closing copy from the current paper, and use compact typography for narrow evidence stacks.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Cross-paper validation decks have no high/medium text overflow findings while preserving the candidate style grammar.

trigger_signals: text box center is inside a card/container but estimated rendered text height exceeds the container bottom padding
text capacity ratio is above the overflow threshold inside a shallow evidence card
human screenshot shows text escaping the visual card even though the card rectangle remains in bounds
badcase_rules.root_cause: The renderer used a fixed shallow text box inside the card and did not recompute card/body height after inserting real text.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Resize the evidence card text area, split the copy across cards, or shorten the card body before accepting the slide.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Nonvisual audit reports no text_exceeds_container_bounds finding on evidence-card text.

trigger_signals: native table bbox exceeds the nearest table/evidence container after padding
table bottom or top crosses the straight rectangular carrier
table overflow is visible from PPTX geometry without needing a screenshot
badcase_rules.root_cause: The table renderer fitted rows to the slide but did not verify that the table stayed inside its semantic container.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Resize, split, or reflow the native table inside the container before applying style-specific polish.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Nonvisual audit reports no table_exceeds_container_bounds findings and table row height remains above the readability floor.

trigger_signals: native table has many columns
a high fraction of cells are empty
the visible grid is wide but information is concentrated in a few cramped cells
badcase_rules.root_cause: The table renderer preserved the extracted grid literally, but source table spans or grouped headings were not represented, leaving many empty visible columns.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Collapse empty columns, preserve source table spanning as an image, or split the table into focused stage blocks.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Table pages either preserve readable native table grammar or are routed to a fitted source-table image / focused subtable layout.

trigger_signals: table column width is below the wrapping threshold
one or more non-empty cells contain long words or long text units
human screenshot shows stacked letters or excessive line wrapping inside cells
badcase_rules.root_cause: The table was squeezed into too many narrow native columns, so text wraps vertically and becomes unreadable.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Increase effective column width, reduce visible columns, or render the source table/diagram as a fitted image when native cells become unreadable.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Nonvisual audit reports no table_cell_text_wrapping_risk, or the packet records a human-approved table-image fallback.

trigger_signals: wide evidence panel has sufficient area
inserted picture uses only a small fraction of panel area
large inner margins remain around the figure
caption or label space dominates the readable image area
badcase_rules.root_cause: A style-aware figure repair routed the image into a bottom/wide panel but did not preserve enough readable figure area.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Compare bottom-band and right-panel-large variants under the active style contract, then send the slide to human visual review.
badcase_rules.regression_check: The visual_human_review_packet marks the slide as accepted, rejected, tradeoff_review, or likely_overcorrection before the repair is promoted.

trigger_signals: wide bottom evidence panel contains a figure
caption text sits below the fitted picture
caption paragraph is left-aligned or its center drifts from the evidence panel center
human reviewer says the caption should sit centered under the figure
badcase_rules.root_cause: The figure renderer reused a left-aligned caption treatment inside a centered wide evidence panel.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Center the figure caption across the proof panel under the fitted image.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Wide-panel figure captions use centered paragraph alignment and stay centered under the proof panel.

trigger_signals: table is inside a large evidence panel
native or focused table uses a low fraction of panel area
large top/bottom/side whitespace remains inside the straight rectangle
human reviewer says the table should be larger or moved to the long bottom rectangle
badcase_rules.root_cause: The dense-table fallback preserved readability but kept a small side-panel footprint, leaving the straight rectangle visually underused.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Route dense/long tables into the bottom wide evidence panel or increase the focused table footprint within the evidence panel.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Focused table layouts no longer trigger table_underutilized_in_evidence_panel and avoid sparse-column wrapping findings.

trigger_signals: slide proof type is table
table is visible inside a straight rectangular evidence panel
there is no compact Focused table view label directly above the table
human reviewer prefers the table-specific view label used by dense-table fallback pages
badcase_rules.root_cause: Dense-table fallback had a title treatment, but ordinary native table rendering skipped the same table-view label.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Render a compact Focused table view label above every table evidence object in this style.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Every table evidence page has a non-component Focused table view label above the table.

trigger_signals: slide proof type is table
table has no explanatory note below it
or the note exists but is not center-aligned under the table/panel
paper source contains a table caption, title, or proof focus that should be visible
badcase_rules.root_cause: The table renderer preserved table cells but dropped the table caption/explanation from the visible evidence block.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Use the table caption/title when available, otherwise use proof.focus as a centered table note under the table.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Every table evidence page has a centered short caption or proof-focus note below the table.

trigger_signals: straight rectangular text evidence card has more vertical room than the rendered copy needs
text frame is top anchored instead of vertically centered
human screenshot shows body copy visually glued to the top edge
badcase_rules.root_cause: The previous overflow repair increased evidence-card height but did not change the text frame's vertical anchor.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Middle-anchor text within shallow straight-rectangle evidence cards, or reduce card height when content is short.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Text evidence cards with vertical slack use middle vertical anchoring and no longer trigger top-heavy alignment findings.

trigger_signals: iteration-level machine finding count decreases
removed findings include a style-aware layout rule
added findings include image_underutilized_in_wide_panel or another visual readability risk
human reviewer says the before layout looked better
badcase_rules.root_cause: The repair optimized metadata counts without respecting the active style contract or human-visible figure readability.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Do not count the repair as accepted until the visual_human_review_packet is approved; if rejected, convert the case into a scoped rule.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Repair logs include page_level_audit_delta and a human_outcome before promotion.

trigger_signals: figure proof object has an image aspect ratio above the wide-figure threshold
layout family is still visual_left or visual_right
figure is inserted with both fixed width and fixed height that do not match the original aspect ratio
badcase_rules.root_cause: The renderer treated all figures as the same proof-object type and ignored the source image shape when choosing the component frame.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Compute figure aspect ratio from the extracted asset and route very wide figures to a long bottom proof panel; fit the image inside the box without distortion.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Very wide figure assets use figure_bottom_wide or another horizontal figure layout, and inserted picture dimensions preserve the source aspect ratio.

trigger_signals: figure proof object has a tall or medium-wide source image aspect ratio
the containing rounded proof panel has a near-square or opposite-aspect frame
picture aspect is preserved but the image remains too small because the panel shape is wrong
figure labels occupy a top header row that reduces the image viewport
badcase_rules.root_cause: The layout router matched only proof type and ultra-wide figures, but did not treat source image shape as part of the component contract.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Route tall figures to vertical side proof panels, route only clearly-wide figures to bottom horizontal panels, and keep labels as compact annotations that do not steer image centering.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Tall figures use figure_tall_left/right when the active style contract matches rounded proof-panel grammar; rectangular right-panel layouts require human review before bottom-band repair is accepted.

trigger_signals: figure image center is materially offset from the containing proof panel center
figure label rail or reserved label area pushes the image to one side
caption width is constrained by label space instead of spanning the proof panel
badcase_rules.root_cause: A label rail was treated as a layout column instead of a compact annotation, so the image no longer read as the centered subject of the rounded panel.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Center the image using the full proof panel content box; place FIGURE/Figure N as a compact top/corner annotation; center the caption across the proof panel width.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Figure picture center stays within the configured panel-center tolerance and captions are not narrowed by label columns.

trigger_signals: Figure N identity labels are anchored to the rounded panel corner instead of the fitted image edge
bottom-wide figure panels show a large blank gap above the image because the Figure N row owns unrelated panel space
visual_left or visual_right figure panels use a generic proof-object title row instead of the fitted-image label anchor
Figure N identity labels are not horizontally centered above the fitted image
badcase_rules.root_cause: The renderer placed the figure identity label before computing the actual image fit, so the identity label could pull the viewer's optical center away from the figure.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Fit the image first, place Figure N horizontally centered above the fitted image, keep the green FIGURE badge at the rounded panel's top-left corner, and keep captions as fixed-height centered annotations.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Figure N labels are horizontal, outside the image, centered above the fitted picture, and separated from the green FIGURE badge; caption boxes do not auto-grow outside the panel.

trigger_signals: Figure N label box center matches the fitted image center but the visible text appears left-shifted
paragraph alignment is not center inside an image-centered Figure N textbox
ordinary figure proof panels render Figure N as a wide left-aligned row even though the row spans the image width
reviewer says the Figure N label is centered to the wrong visual target even though the bbox geometry passes
badcase_rules.root_cause: The renderer centered the textbox over the fitted image but left the paragraph alignment at its default left alignment.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Center-align the Figure N paragraph inside the textbox after centering the textbox over the fitted image.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Metadata audit reports no figure_label_text_alignment_off_center findings in dedicated figure panels, including standard visual_left/right figure proof panels.

trigger_signals: black proof identity labels such as Motivation, Method, Doc Table 1, or Table 2 sit near the panel type badge instead of above the panel content center
text-evidence strip labels are centered to the header row rather than the explanation text box
table proof labels are not centered over the table body
badcase_rules.root_cause: The renderer treated proof identity labels as header-row text near the green type badge instead of anchoring them to the proof content they identify.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Keep the green type badge at the panel corner, but center the black identity label over the underlying table, metric, image, or explanation text box.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Metadata audit reports no panel_identity_label_anchor_drift findings in rounded proof panels.

trigger_signals: proof identity label textbox is centered over the table or explanation text, but the visible label remains left-shifted
paragraph alignment is not center inside a content-centered proof identity label textbox
Doc Table or Table labels appear visually attached to the left edge of the panel title row
badcase_rules.root_cause: The label textbox geometry matched the content center, but the paragraph retained the default left alignment.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Center-align proof identity label paragraphs after aligning their textbox to the main proof content.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Metadata audit reports no panel_identity_label_text_alignment_off_center findings in rounded proof panels.

trigger_signals: green FIGURE badge is placed above the fitted image instead of inside the rounded panel's top-left corner
green FIGURE badge and black Figure N identity label share one crowded horizontal row
Figure N label is merged with the green FIGURE badge instead of staying as a separate image-corner label
badcase_rules.root_cause: The renderer treated the component type badge and the source figure identity label as one label cluster, even though they explain different visual entities.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Separate the two label semantics: pin FIGURE to the proof panel's inner top-left corner, and place Figure N horizontally above the fitted image centerline.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Metadata audit reports no figure_badge_identity_label_conflation findings: FIGURE has a small panel-corner inset, and Figure N is a separate horizontal image-corner label.

trigger_signals: Figure N is rendered as true stacked F/I/G/U/R/E/N text
human reviewer says the stacked label looks worse than the horizontal image-corner label
a literal vertical-text repair reduces visual elegance despite fixing label crowding
badcase_rules.root_cause: The repair interpreted vertical placement too literally and optimized semantics at the expense of visual taste.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Use horizontal Figure N text just above and centered with the fitted image; keep it outside the image and separated from the green FIGURE panel badge.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Metadata audit reports no stacked_figure_identity_label_overcorrection findings in dedicated figure panels.

trigger_signals: PPTX picture shape aspect ratio differs materially from the embedded source image aspect ratio
figure was inserted with both fixed width and fixed height instead of a fitted aspect-preserving box
human reviewer describes the figure as squeezed, stretched, or unclear after resizing
badcase_rules.root_cause: The renderer filled the component viewport by forcing picture width and height rather than fitting the source image into the available box.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Compute a centered fit rectangle from source image dimensions and component content bounds; supply fitted width and height that preserve the source aspect ratio.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Nonvisual audit reports no figure_picture_aspect_distortion findings for generated figure proof panels.

trigger_signals: original academic slide uses Key message plus a bottom full-width table
upper-right evidence region contains no meaningful metric, note, figure, or proof object
slide spec has table and metrics but renderer leaves the right evidence region blank
badcase_rules.root_cause: The original academic visual-or-mixed renderer rendered the bottom table before its metric fallback, so table+metric/no-image pages skipped the right metric/evidence column.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: For original academic table+metric/no-image pages, render metric cards in the right evidence region; when no metrics exist, render compact evidence notes instead.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Nonvisual audit reports no academic_right_evidence_void findings on AGI Wordle slides 9 and 13, and golden_baseline1 scoped audits are unchanged.

trigger_signals: original academic Contents slide uses the mature golden-baseline TOC grammar
the TOC lists only four modules instead of the six-module paper-reading route
Analysis or Ablations is missing from the Contents page
badcase_rules.root_cause: The renderer derived the original academic TOC directly from compacted slide section labels, so LLM-curated specs that merged analysis/ablation material into Results collapsed the mature six-module route.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: For the protected original academic style, render the Contents page with Motivation, Method, Analysis, Ablations, Results, and Conclusion when the deck is a paper-reading academic route.
badcase_rules.regression_check: AGI Wordle academic route slide 2 lists all six canonical sections; golden_baseline1 Roadmap remains scoped to its own module grammar.

trigger_signals: slide proof object references a table by display title rather than extracted asset id
slide_spec inline table contains rows but table_index lookup returns no rows
table proof panel renders as a fallback text block instead of a native table
badcase_rules.root_cause: The proof-object resolver could select curated slide tables, but the table renderer only indexed extracted asset tables.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Index curated inline table rows together with extracted table assets before rendering and auditing table proof objects.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Title-referenced inline tables render as native PPT tables with row/column grammar instead of empty-looking text panels.

trigger_signals: paper title contains a Unicode ellipsis inside the title rather than at the end
semantic QA reports truncated ellipsis even though the title is a real source title
example: AGI Is Coming… Right After AI Learns to Play Wordle
badcase_rules.root_cause: The truncated-ellipsis detector treated any Unicode ellipsis followed by a capitalized word as generated truncation.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Continue flagging three-dot ellipses and trailing Unicode ellipses, but allow in-title Unicode ellipses from source paper titles.
badcase_rules.regression_check: QA does not flag AGI Is Coming… Right After AI Learns to Play Wordle, while still flagging trailing ellipses.

trigger_signals: academic global repair route rerenders a modified spec but raw nonvisual finding counts do not improve
repair log records copy fitting yet second audit has the same high and medium count
layout QA passes while metadata audit still reports typography and overlap risks
badcase_rules.root_cause: The repair action compacted generic spec fields but did not target the exact rendered text boxes or layout family signals named by nonvisual audit.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Map nonvisual findings back to slide spec fields and renderer components before claiming global repair success; otherwise report the route as unresolved.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Benchmark curve must show lower blocking findings after global repair, or the report must mark the repair as unresolved.

trigger_signals: blind experimental route improves low/medium counts but high estimated_text_overflow remains
new style uses independent visual grammar but lacks a complete text fitting strategy
support_body or card_text remains above capacity after one bounded repair pass
badcase_rules.root_cause: The blind renderer changed visual grammar and figure frame routing, but its text allocation still uses fixed boxes that are too small for AGI Wordle support text.
badcase_rules.repair_strategy: Add a third repair pass that either splits dense support into paired cards, raises box height, or moves secondary detail to speaker notes while preserving the blueprint style contract.
badcase_rules.regression_check: Blind route should reduce high text-capacity findings across iterations before being presented as a finished third style.

good_signals: title, agenda, section, content, and closing slides feel intentional
deck looks like an academic presentation rather than generated notes
restrained but lively warm academic colors
proof objects can appear right, bottom, compact, table, metric, or mosaic depending on content
bad_signals: same right proof panel on most pages
left evidence triplets on formal pages if they reduce gravitas

good_signals: wide figures use frames that respect their original shape
metrics preserve value, label, and context
text evidence uses appropriately sized cards
bad_signals: wide figures are squeezed into side panels or distorted

good_signals: title, claim, support, card text, table text, and footer have clear hierarchy
sparse text does not create awkward empty containers
component frames adapt after content fitting without changing deck-wide type roles
bad_signals: card text too sparse for card size
label/body stacks or proof labels feel visually detached from their component

good_signals: visual audit manifest identifies high-risk pages
text snapshots or rendered screenshots are produced when possible
bad_signals: system cannot inspect generated deck artifacts

good_signals: from-scratch deck does not copy golden baseline skeleton
new visual system preserves parsed paper content

autonomous_generation_workflow.goal: Reuse parsed checkpoints to collect paper metadata, thesis, highlights, sections, figures, tables, metrics, and evidence links.
non_visual_checks: required checkpoint files exist
paper title and author/team are present
figures, tables, and metrics have stable identifiers
core sections cover motivation, method, experiments, and takeaway
autonomous_generation_workflow.default_repair: Return to inventory construction; do not redesign slides until missing evidence is recovered from existing checkpoints.

autonomous_generation_workflow.goal: Decide that the output is an academic paper-reading deck with title, agenda, section dividers, content modules, and closing slide.
non_visual_checks: slide roles include title, agenda, section_opener, content roles, and closing
agenda modules map to contiguous slide ranges
section counts are plausible for the requested slide budget
autonomous_generation_workflow.default_repair: Regenerate section buckets and slide-role map before touching visual components.

autonomous_generation_workflow.goal: Assign one main claim, concise support text, and one matching proof object to each content slide.
non_visual_checks: each content slide has exactly one dominant claim
support text is not empty and is not a duplicate of the claim
proof object type matches the slide role
table, figure, and metric slides retain source references
title-referenced inline tables with rows remain renderable proof payloads
autonomous_generation_workflow.default_repair: Repair slide spec content first; do not hide semantic gaps with layout decoration.

autonomous_generation_workflow.goal: Define palette, typography hierarchy, layout families, evidence card grammar, metric grammar, table grammar, and forbidden baseline-like skeletons.
non_visual_checks: layout family distribution is varied but not random
accepted component proportions are preserved unless a structural rule fails
colors and component roles follow the style contract
new deck does not collapse into the golden baseline macro skeleton
autonomous_generation_workflow.default_repair: Change style tokens or layout assignment rules; avoid ad-hoc per-slide resizing as the first fix.

autonomous_generation_workflow.goal: Insert real slide text into the chosen components, then adjust only components whose fitted text makes them visibly too empty, too full, detached, or boundary-unsafe.
non_visual_checks: paired label/body stacks use stable local gaps
2x2 flow grids keep compact columns, breathable rows, and centered labels
agenda read-path header keeps enough clearance above the flow nodes
table-bottom support copy stays closer to the claim than to the table proof panel
component frames are not substantially overallocated after fitted text height is estimated
shallow evidence cards scale internal label/body spacing to local card height
figure/table labels clear rounded component boundaries
very wide figures are assigned a horizontal proof frame instead of a side frame
autonomous_generation_workflow.default_repair: Resize or reposition the local component and its same-slide siblings; preserve deck-wide type roles and avoid changing unrelated pages.

autonomous_generation_workflow.goal: Inspect generated PPTX as a layout program: shape geometry, font sizes, text capacity, table grammar, metric grammar, and overlap risk.
non_visual_checks: no high-risk text/proof/table overlap
font-size floors pass by role
near-capacity and low-density findings are classified separately
tables preserve rows and columns
inline table rows from slide_spec are indexed when no extracted table id matches
wide figure images preserve source aspect ratio when fitted into PPTX picture boxes
metrics preserve value, label, and context
original academic bottom-table pages fill the upper-right evidence region when no figure is present
table-bottom claim/support/table-panel spacing passes local text-band balance checks
paired text stacks, shallow-card internal spacing, component frame fit, and component boundary inset pass local optical checks
autonomous_generation_workflow.default_repair: Emit badcase hits and rank only the top issues for the next repair pass.

autonomous_generation_workflow.goal: Repair the highest-impact problems without breaking the accepted overall composition.
non_visual_checks: repair changes are limited to top 1-3 badcases
copy and font fixes are preferred before resizing accepted components
component geometry changes require a structural or content-fit failure such as overlap, unreadable table, missing content, failed flow grid, boundary violation, or overallocated frame
same-slide sibling components are reflowed after any local frame resize
new output is compared against accepted-reference rules
autonomous_generation_workflow.default_repair: Stop when high/medium findings are gone or when another repair would alter the style contract without evidence.

autonomous_generation_workflow.goal: Before promoting a successful style to a golden baseline, rerun it on papers with different figure, table, metric, and text-evidence profiles.
non_visual_checks: candidate style passes nonvisual audit without high or medium findings on each validation paper
new findings are separated into style-specific failures versus paper-content extraction failures
human reviewer approves the contact-sheet rhythm on at least two non-primary papers
every recurring cross-paper complaint becomes a badcase before promotion
autonomous_generation_workflow.default_repair: Keep the style as a candidate reference, add or tune badcases, and rerun validation instead of declaring a golden baseline from one paper.

non_visual_self_repair_policy.design_assumption: Treat PPTX as a structured layout program. The system cannot literally see the slide, but it can inspect the objects, positions, sizes, fonts, text length, tables, and role metadata that produce the slide.
detectable_without_screenshots: missing title, agenda, section, or closing roles
agenda modules not aligned with slide ranges
claim/support/proof object missing or mismatched
shape bounding-box overlap and out-of-bounds objects
font-size floors and inconsistent typography hierarchy
deck-level typography comfort band across repeated text roles
text capacity, near-overflow risk, and low-density card/panel risk
paired label/body stack proximity for cover highlights and card-like groups
flow-node crowding, automatic two-row flow needs, grid proportions, and label-center drift
agenda read-path header clearance above P/M/E/T flow nodes
table-bottom support proximity to the claim and clearance above the table panel
component frame overallocation after fitted text height is estimated
shallow evidence card label/body gap and bottom padding
component label boundary inset for figure/table proof panels
figure source aspect ratio and whether the chosen layout family matches it
inserted figure picture box aspect ratio versus source image aspect ratio
original academic bottom-table pages with a missing right evidence column
container internal stack optical balance and metric value-label gap
native table row/column availability
curated inline table row/column availability when table ids do not match extracted assets
metric value/label/context grammar
layout-family repetition and monotony
use of forbidden or risky visual grammar recorded from human feedback
not_reliably_detectable_without_screensh: subtle beauty of color interaction after rendering
human emotional preference when two valid compositions differ
font rendering differences across PowerPoint installations
repair_priority_ladder: Fix content correctness first: missing evidence, unsupported claims, table rows, metric values.
Fix structural deck grammar second: title, agenda, section ranges, slide role balance.
Fix semantic matching third: claim/support/proof object alignment.
Fix typography fourth: font floors, deck-level comfort band, text splitting, line breaks, copy allocation.
Fix content-fit optical balance fifth: paired label/body proximity, table support band balance, value-label gap, card padding, and proof-label boundary inset.
Fix local component frame sizing sixth when fitted text makes a card clearly too empty or too full; then reflow same-slide siblings.
Fix geometry only when necessary: overlap, out-of-bounds, unreadable table, failed flow grid, boundary inset violation, or repeated layout family.
Change accepted component proportions only when the audit shows a structural or content-fit failure, not merely low text density.
Change the visual system only through a new style-contract revision and compare against the accepted reference.
stop_conditions: no high or medium non-visual findings remain
remaining findings are low-density or low-font risks that would require style-contract changes
a repair would improve local density but violate accepted-reference composition
content_score, visual_layout_score, and nonvisual audit are stable across two attempts

cheap_non_visual_checks: slide roles present: title, agenda, sections, content, closing
layout family distribution and max consecutive layout
shape bounding box overlap among text, tables, figures, and proof panels
deck-level typography comfort band by repeated roles
text density: words per square inch for cards and panels
flow-node label gap, two-row fallback need, grid gap ratio, and label-center drift
component frame extra height after fitted text estimate
component label boundary inset for figure/table panels
container internal padding balance and metric value-label stack gap
table row/column availability and native table count
disabled_render_checks_for_current_phase: one section divider per visual family
metric pages with low label/context confidence
pages flagged by non-visual overlap or density checks

vision_judge_policy.default: Disabled for the current phase. Do not judge slides with a vision model unless the user explicitly reopens that route.
when_to_call: explicit user request to compare rendered pages
expected_output: whether change improves or regresses from accepted reference
